Headline The complex processed 1,578.6 kt of ore at 25.2 % P2O5 and delivered 544.5 kt of Dap at 18.1 % N, recovering 82.8 % of the P2O5 of the ore. The acid train digested 334.5 kt of P2O5 with 2.85 t of sulphuric acid per tonne, the filters lost 2.34 % of it in the gypsum and the evaporators spent 0.4075 t of steam per tonne. The tonne of product cost 396.6 :USD in variable cost and carried 55.92 kgCO2e per tonne of P2O5. The detector raised 63 findings worth 7.7162261e7 :USD a year, and the plant is Noncompliant against 42 clauses of 9 frameworks.

Phosphoric acid: balance, specification and cost

The acid plant produced 142.1 kt of merchant acid -- 79.2 kt P2O5, 109.4 kt H3PO4 on the 100 % basis -- at 55.74 % P2O5, which is the :technical grade. The evaporators removed 507 thousand t of water with 0.41729 t of steam per t of P2O5 concentrated, an economy of 3.72 t of water per t of steam. The acid leaves the plant Compliant against the specification of the traded grade.

The digital twin: steady state, limits and alignment

The steady-state twin of the reaction train is a square system of 15 nonlinear balances solved with ModelingToolkit (ModelingToolkit nonlinear balance, mtkcompile + NonlinearProblem). It converged in 12.13 s with a largest residual of 0.0 -- the residual is reported because a solution nobody checked is a guess.

Predictive control of the reaction train

The controller is the one the plant would run: a linear predictive controller over the discrete model 11 x 11 obtained by linearising the ODE twin at its operating point (12 prediction steps, 4 control steps, sample time 1 h), with a Kalman filter estimating the states from the measurements. The plant of the test is the nonlinear twin, so the controller never sees the equations it is controlling.

Optimisation of the blend, the operating point and the sourcing

Three models of the same plant are solved every day: the blend of the ore the digester is fed -- a linear program over the registered assays with the specifications of the reaction section --, the operating point of the reaction train -- a nonlinear program over the correlations of the twin -- and the annual sourcing plan, a mixed-integer program because a body is bought by the shipload.

  • The **design** of the plant is registered in `process.jl`: capacities, targets, the flowsheet and the instrument register. Every model of the package reads it, so a capacity change propagates to the twin, the optimiser, the controller and the report.
  • The **campaign** is a seeded grey-box model of that design (`plantdata.jl`): the production schedule, the ore blend, the weather and the injected deviations are all functions of the seed, so every figure and every PDF can be reproduced from the seed printed on the cover page.
  • The **stoichiometry** is computed from the molar masses in `measures.jl`: 2.3 t of H2SO4 and 4.04 t of gypsum per tonne of P2O5 in fluorapatite, plus the demand of the free carbonate of the ore. The assays of the ore bodies are representative published figures, not the assay of a particular mine.
  • The **twin** is written in ModelingToolkit: a square nonlinear balance of 15 unknowns for the steady state, and 11 differential equations on an hourly clock for the dynamics. Both report the residual of every equation they solve.
  • The **controller** is a linear MPC over the linearised twin with a Kalman filter, closed on the nonlinear twin as the plant; the baseline is a PI controller tuned on the same steady-state gains, so the comparison is like for like.
  • The **soft sensors** are linear models of the variables that are measured slowly or not at all, validated on a holdout and equipped with an applicability domain: outside the conditions they were fitted on, they report that they cannot answer.
  • The **cost and carbon** of the site use the register of `process.jl` (:USD) and the factors of the GHG Protocol: 0.371 kgCO2e/kWh for the grid and 50.29 kgCO2e/GJ for the fuel.
